Welcome

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.1 Quick Reference
  • HTML Living Standard
  • A11y 101

content.text:
I made a handful of improvements to `0.html`, but the most important problem is not fixed: the page's CSP style hash is invalid, so browsers will block the entire stylesheet and render the page unstyled.

## Needs your action: the CSP hash

The `style-src` hash on line 5 is 43 characters long; a base64 SHA-256 is always 44, so it cannot match any stylesheet. This was already broken before my edits. I couldn't regenerate it because running the hash command was blocked in this session (no approval available), and nothing has been tested in a browser.

To fix it, run this in the directory and paste the output in place of the existing `sha256-...` value:

```sh
python3 -c "import re,hashlib,base64;s=open('0.html',encoding='utf-8').read();print('sha256-'+base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(re.search(r'<style>(.*?)</style>',s,re.S).group(1).encode()).digest()).decode())"
```

The hash covers the exact bytes between `<style>` and `</style>`, so it has to be regenerated after any CSS edit, including whitespace. Chrome's console also prints the expected hash in its CSP violation message.

## What I changed

- **Print colours:** print styles now force a light palette, so printing from dark mode no longer puts light grey text on white paper. The button is also hidden in print.
- **Button transition:** `transition: all` is replaced with `opacity` and `transform` only, the two properties that actually change.
- **Button type:** the button now has `type="button"`, so it won't submit if it ever ends up inside a form.
- **Section labels:** the Features, Examples and Resources sections now have `aria-labelledby` pointing at their headings, so they are exposed as named regions to screen readers.

## Left alone

- **Placeholder URLs:** the canonical, `og:url` and `og:image` values still point to `example.com`; replace them with the real ones before publishing.
- **Author email:** `meta name="author"` holds your email address on a page marked `index, follow`, which makes it harvestable by scrapers. Consider using a name instead.
- **"Learn More" button:** it does nothing, and the CSP blocks all scripts. If it is meant to go somewhere, it should be a link.
